000
FXUS63 KIWX 101035
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
635 AM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Periods of light rain expected this evening into Sunday 
  morning, especially east of Interstate 69 where up to a half 
  an inch of rain may fall. 

- An active pattern sets up for the second half of next week
  with gusty winds, showers and possible thunderstorms, then 
  turning colder into next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 208 AM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Another day of well above normal temperatures is in store as some 
WAA continues. Remnants of "Isaias" will continue slowly north 
through the day and eventually more northeast tonight into Sunday. 
Bands of cirrus will work across the area, generally thin in nature 
until the circulation edges closer. Scattered showers may quickly 
move north across much of the area near/after 3Z Sun then steadier 
precip arriving after 6Z and lingering along and east of Interstate 
69. QPF is somewhat lower than past days with amounts possibly at 
most less than one half inch. Model blends still keeping some slgt 
chc pops for thunder. Lapse rates not overly impressive, but some 
elevated instability is noted (negative Showalters). Will leave in 
for the time being. 

With regards to temps on Sunday, some guidance suggests high temps 
could be several degrees cooler (mainly east) which could have some 
validity with the extensive cloud cover and precip. These temps seem 
to be in the lower percentile range, so have left previous highs 
alone and pass onto the next shift. 

Lull in precip chances arrives Sunday night into Monday, before a 
series of weak waves and fronts arrive for mid week. Thereafter, med 
range models have sort of diverged some on the degree of phasing of 
a weaker northern and stronger southern stream wave. Pops remain in 
place with signs still pointing towards cooling for the weekend, but 
the degree of cooling and amount of precip is in question with these 
variations.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 635 AM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Mid/upper level clouds will continue to increase today but
relatively dry low levels will maintain VFR conditions. Light
rain showers expected at KFWA after 06Z tonight with some MVFR 
ceilings likely closer to 12Z Sunday as tropical moisture plume
lifts north. There is also a low (20%) chance of an embedded 
thunderstorm but not worth including in the TAF at this point.
Dry/VFR conditions expected to persist at KSBN given eastward
displacement of better moisture.


&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Fisher
AVIATION...AGD

spc.text:
SPC AC 100554

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1254 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE EASTERN FLORIDA PANHANDLE...GEORGIA AND SOUTH CAROLINA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms associated with a tornado threat will be possible
   today from the eastern Florida Panhandle northeastward into the
   Carolinas. A few severe wind gusts may also occur in parts of the
   Desert Southwest.

   ...Eastern Florida Panhandle/Georgia/Carolinas...
   The remnants of Isaias are forecast to move northward into the
   Tennessee Valley today. The eastern extent of the system will move
   north-northeastward across Georgia and South Carolina today, where
   isolated to scattered thunderstorms will develop as surface
   temperatures warm. From eastern Georgia into South Carolina, surface
   dewpoints in the mid to upper 70s F will contribute to moderate
   instability, with MLCAPE likely peaking in the 1500 to 2000 J/kg
   range. RAP forecast soundings along and near the axis of instability
   this afternoon have veering winds with height below 850 mb and 30 to
   40 knot of flow in the low to mid-levels. 0-3 km storm-relative
   helicity is forecast to peak near 225 m2/s2. This will support a
   tornado threat with supercells that remain semi-discrete. The
   tornado threat is expected to persist into the evening as the
   eastern periphery of Isaias moves into the Carolinas. 

   ...Western and Southern Arizona/Southeast California...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will move northeastward toward Baja
   California today, with the system interacting with Tropical Storm
   Rachel. Ahead of the system, low-level moisture advection will
   increase surface dewpoints into the 60s F over much of western and
   southern Arizona by this evening. In response, MLCAPE is forecast to
   increase to near 1000 J/kg over parts of southwest Arizona. This
   combined with large-scale ascent ahead of the system and lift
   associated with a low-level jet will provide support for scattered
   thunderstorm development. In addition, the exit region of a
   mid-level jet is forecast to overspread southwest Arizona during the
   evening. This feature will create moderate to strong deep-layer
   shear, which will be sufficient for supercells. If a supercell can
   develop, then isolated severe wind gusts would be possible.

   ..Broyles/Chalmers.. 10/10/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Widely scattered severe storms capable of a few tornadoes and damaging wind gusts appear possible over portions of North Carolina, Virginia, and southeast Maryland Sunday afternoon and evening. A brief tornado or two may occur over portions of the lower Colorado Valley Sunday morning, with sporadic occurrences of severe wind gusts possible into the Great Basin and central Rockies Sunday afternoon and evening.
spc.text:
SPC AC 100532

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1232 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PORTIONS OF
   NORTH CAROLINA...VIRGINIA...AND SOUTHEAST MARYLAND...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Widely scattered severe storms capable of a few tornadoes and
   damaging wind gusts appear possible over portions of North Carolina,
   Virginia, and southeast Maryland Sunday afternoon and evening. A
   brief tornado or two may occur over portions of the lower Colorado
   Valley Sunday morning, with sporadic occurrences of severe wind
   gusts possible into the Great Basin and central Rockies Sunday
   afternoon and evening.

   ...Synopsis...

   A mid/upper-level low over KY and TN Sunday morning is forecast to
   evolve into an open wave while progressing into the Mid-Atlantic by
   Sunday night. That system will be preceded by a focused corridor of
   height falls and a belt of 45-55+ kt southwesterly flow in the
   midlevels, which will overspread the Carolinas and southern
   Mid-Atlantic during the day. While the primary surface low will
   remain displaced to the northwest of the warm sector, secondary
   cyclogenesis is forecast during the afternoon over central VA at the
   junction of a cool front/trough advancing east from the Blue Ridge
   and a warm front lifting north into the Mid-Atlantic.

   Elsewhere, the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel will weaken while
   accelerating from southern CA into the Great Basin within a belt of
   50-60 kt midlevel flow. The associated surface circulation/low will
   likewise develop from southern CA into northern UT by Sunday
   evening.


   ...Southern Mid-Atlantic into the Carolinas...

   A 40-45 kt low-level jet will persist over the Piedmont and Coastal
   Plain, enhancing the poleward transport of a moist boundary layer,
   characterized by dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s. Showers and
   thunderstorms are likely to be ongoing at 12Z Sunday within the
   expanding warm sector with lingering clouds and areas of
   precipitation limiting daytime heating and resultant destabilization
   at many locations. Nonetheless, a moist and at least marginally
   unstable air mass will coincide with strengthening low-level and
   deep-layer shear, which may support transient supercells with the
   threat for a brief tornado or two and/or strong wind gusts spreading
   from the Carolinas into the southern Mid-Atlantic on Sunday.  

   A higher-probability risk for sustained supercells capable of a few
   tornadoes and damaging winds may materialize by afternoon into
   evening from portions of central and eastern NC into south-central
   into southeast VA, where the 00Z REFS and HREF guidance indicates a
   corridor of locally stronger instability (SBCAPE up to 1000-1250
   J/kg). Those areas have been upgraded to 5% tornado and 15% wind
   probabilities and a related Level-2/Slight Risk.  
     

   ...Lower Colorado Valley into the Great Basin and central Rockies...


   A low-level moisture plume (e.g., dewpoints in the mid 50s to
   mid-upper 60s) originating from the Gulf of CA will reside over the
   lower-CO Valley Sunday morning, with REFS and HREF guidance
   indicating SBCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg. Relatively strong vertical
   shear, aided by the low-level mass response to the remnant Rachel
   circulation, will be more than sufficient for supercells and bowing
   structures capable of isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a brief
   tornado or two over the lower-CO Valley Sunday morning.

   As mentioned in the synopsis, the system will weaken through the
   day, leading to greater uncertainty in the extent of any associated
   severe weather threat during the afternoon into evening. That said,
   corridors of modest instability are expected to develop across
   portions of the Great Basin into the central Rockies, which combined
   with relatively strong cloud-bearing shear will be supportive of
   widely scattered severe storms capable of mainly severe wind gusts.

   ..Mead.. 10/10/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.summary: No severe weather is expected Monday through Monday night.
spc.text:
SPC AC 100721

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0221 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026

   Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe weather is expected Monday through Monday night.

   ...Synopsis...

   A midlevel low initially over the Columbia Basin is forecast to
   progress south toward the Sierra Nevada, while an upper-level jet
   streak develops from the lower-CO Valley into the Upper Midwest.
   Ahead of the latter feature, a low-amplitude short-wave trough is
   projected to move from the northern High Plains into the Upper
   Midwest, embedded within a belt of 40-50 kt midlevel flow. In the
   low levels, an area of low pressure loosely related to the
   short-wave trough is expected to develop from the mid-MO Valley into
   the Upper Midwest along a stationary front. A cold front will trail
   southwest from that feature, linking with a secondary cyclone over
   the central High Plains.

   ...Upper Midwest/Upper Great Lakes...

   A plume of relatively steep midlevel lapse rates of around 7 C/km
   will overlie the northern extension of a moistening boundary layer,
   supporting a corridor of moderate instability by afternoon to the
   south of the surface low and associated front described in the
   synopsis. Capping at the base of the lapse-rate plume/EML is likely
   to inhibit surface-based storm development in the warm sector.
   However, the 00Z models suggest that a cluster of elevated
   thunderstorms may persist Monday afternoon into night to the
   immediate north of the warm sector within a zone of forcing for
   ascent preceding the short-wave trough. While a few strong storms
   capable of small hail appear possible, marginal parcel buoyancy and
   only modest cloud-bearing shear are expected to limit the threat for
   severe weather.

   ..Mead.. 10/10/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
